Venison Snack Stick Recipe Guide: Master the Art of Homemade Wild Game Snacks

Introduction to Snack Stick Making

Snack sticks are one of the most convenient, flavorful, and protein-rich snacks you can make at home. Whether you’re a seasoned hunter or just a wild game enthusiast, learning how to craft your own venison snack sticks opens up a world of culinary satisfaction. In this guide, we’ll explore everything from meat preparation, seasoning blends, and stuffing techniques to smoking methods and achieving the perfect internal temperature.

Understanding Venison as a Snack Stick Base

Why Choose Venison?

Venison, or deer meat, is lean, high in protein, and a favorite among those who enjoy wild game. When used in snack sticks, venison provides a rich, earthy flavor that pairs perfectly with spice, cure, and smoke.

Meat to Fat Ratio Matters

For ideal texture and taste, a meat to fat ratio of 80/20 is recommended. Because lean venison is typically very low in fat, mixing it with pork butt or beef fat can balance the final meat mixture.

Essential Equipment for Homemade Venison Snack Sticks

Grinder and Mixer

A meat grinder with a medium plate (around 4.5 mm) is perfect for a coarse grind that gives texture without being overly chunky. A meat mixer helps ensure uniform seasoning distribution.

Sausage Stuffer and Casings

Use a sausage stuffer to load your collagen casings or mahogany collagen tubes. These materials are ideal for snack sticks because of their strength and smoke permeability.

Smoker or Dehydrator

You can use an electric smoker, pellet smoker, or dehydrator depending on your preference. A smoker using hickory wood imparts a deep, smoky tang that complements smoked venison snack sticks beautifully. Learn more about different types of smokers here.

Venison Snack Stick Seasoning and Ingredients

Core Ingredients

  • Ground venison (5 lbs)
  • Pork butt or beef fat (1-2 lbs)
  • Snack stick seasoning blend
  • Cure #1 (Prague powder)
  • Black pepper / cracked pepper
  • Encapsulated citric acid (for tang and shelf stability)
  • Cheddar cheese or pepper jack (high-temp cheese)
  • Collagen casings

Tip: Always use high temp cheese when adding to snack sticks to avoid melting and oozing during smoking.

Optional Additions

  • Jerky seasoning for extra depth
  • Powdered garlic, onion, or mustard seed
  • Hi Mountain blends for regional flavor profiles

Preparing the Meat Mixture

Step-by-Step Process

  1. Grind your venison and fat through the medium plate.
  2. In a mixer, add your seasoning, cure, cheese, and encapsulated citric acid.
  3. Mix thoroughly until the meat becomes tacky.
  4. Stuff the mixture into collagen casings using a sausage stuffer.
  5. Let the sticks rest overnight in the refrigerator to set the flavors.

Smoking Your Snack Sticks

Smoking Method

  1. Preheat your electric smoker to 130°F and hang or lay your snack sticks inside.
  2. Gradually increase the temp to 180°F over 2-3 hours.
  3. Maintain that temperature until sticks reach an internal temperature of 160°F.
  4. Remove the sticks and place them immediately in an ice bath to stop the cooking process and prevent overcook.

After Smoking

Allow the smoked venison snack sticks to dry at room temperature for 1 hour. You can also use a fan to speed up the process and achieve a drier snack stick texture.

Storage and Packaging

Vacuum Seal and Refrigerate

Once dry, vacuum seal your sticks or store in airtight containers. Refrigerated, they’ll last up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze them.

Dehydrate for Shelf Stability

Using a dehydrator to remove moisture will improve shelf life. This process results in a jerky-like texture, perfect for long hunts or camping.

Variations and Flavor Profiles

Cracked Pepper & Cheddar Venison Snack Sticks

Combine cracked pepper and high-temp cheddar cheese for a sharp, savory punch.

Tangy Summer Sausage Style

Add encapsulated citric acid, mustard seed, and garlic for a summer sausage flavor.

Pepper Jack Explosion

Use pepper jack cheese and hickory smoke for a bold, spicy snack.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Overcook: Always monitor internal temperature with a reliable meat thermometer.
  • Poor mix: Inadequate mixing leads to uneven flavor distribution.
  • Skipping cure: Always use curing salt when cold smoking or slow drying.
  • Improper casing: Use collagen or natural sausage casings specifically made for snack sticks.

Sourcing Ingredients and Tools

Visit your local butcher for fresh deer meat or pork butt. Many also offer custom grind and stuffing services. For DIY, online stores like LEM offer top-quality jerky tools and supplies. Find a guide to choosing LEM grinders and stuffers.

The Final Bite: Your Homemade Venison Snack Stick Recipe

Recap of Key Points:

  • Use a proper meat to fat ratio.
  • Choose high-quality seasoning blends and casings.
  • Monitor smoke temperature and achieve a safe internal temperature.
  • Use an ice bath after cooking to maintain texture.
  • Store via vacuum seal or dehydrator.

With patience, attention to detail, and respect for the craft, you’ll be able to produce a finished product that rivals any store-bought meat sticks—all from the comfort of your home kitchen.

Whether you’re prepping for the deer hunting season or just want healthier, flavorful snacks, this venison snack stick recipe delivers on all fronts. From wild game lovers to health-conscious eaters, it’s a culinary adventure worth taking.
